samples.summary: Backend enforcement-default flip + service-token identity is scope well past the originating issue, and changes behaviour for existing deployments with no migration step
samples.evidence: The originating issue's scope is recorded in docs/tasks/active/20260907-notes-share-toolbar-todo.md as N1–N8 (mount NotesToolbar on the share route, mobile demotion, viewer view-menu, share-token uploader, session-local prefs), plus the engine divider hit area and the notes.md doc corrections. This diff additionally (a) flips `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` from "unset = shadow" to "unset = enforce" (`isYorkieAuthEnforced`), (b) invents a third webhook identity (`src/yorkie/yorkie-service-token.ts`, `decideService`, `READ_GATED_METHODS`), (c) rewires three ops scripts to per-side JWT secrets, and (d) gates presence writes across sheets/slides/board/pdf/docs. Those are a separate architectural change with an operational consequence outside the codebase: docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md previously documented step 2 of the rollout as "Shadow mode (default)", so any deployment that already registered the webhook methods and left the variable unset silently transitions from allow-all to denying on upgrade. The rewritten Rollout section (lines 232-241) describes the new default but records no upgrade/migration note for deployments currently sitting in the old default, and the paired `assertYorkieAuthEnforced`/`register-templates.ts` gates still demand the literal `true`, so an enforcing-by-default deployment is refused the public tier. The notes-toolbar work and the enforcement flip each stand alone and would be far safer to land separately.

samples.summary: Canonical sharing design doc still states auth-webhook enforcement is off by default, contradicting this change
samples.evidence: docs/design/sharing.md:208-219 says "This is **off by default**. `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` is unset in a stock deployment, which puts the controller in shadow mode … in the default one the client-side `readOnly` flag is the write boundary", and lines 231-235 and 184-186 repeat it. This diff inverts exactly that default and takes care to correct the same wrong claim in docs/design/notes/notes.md and docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md, but leaves the top-level sharing doc — the canonical doc for share-link roles — asserting the opposite. Repo doc discipline (docs/design/README.md "Obsolete docs") is to fold corrections into the canonical subsystem doc, so two canonical docs now give opposite answers to "is a viewer's write refused on a stock deployment?".

samples.summary: New comment in the same PR asserts the shadow-mode default the PR removes
samples.evidence: The block comment added at packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:442-448 says "the Yorkie auth webhook ships in shadow (allow-all) mode by default and so may not refuse the write either", while packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts (added in the same diff) makes enforcement the default and docs/design/notes/notes.md explicitly records that claim as wrong. The rationale a future reader will follow is therefore self-contradictory within one change.

samples.summary: The docs read-only store's rationale keeps the now-false shadow-default claim that its notes sibling corrects
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:35-42 still argues "the Yorkie auth webhook — ships in shadow mode by default … so with the default configuration this flag is the write boundary rather than a convenience in front of one." packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:58-70, added here, explicitly labels that reasoning wrong and rewrites it. The two sibling modules that implement the same boundary now document mutually exclusive premises; the docs copy is the one a reader of the docs package will find.

samples.summary: readOnlyNoteStore duplicates readOnlyDocStore's Proxy machinery near-verbatim instead of sharing one guard
samples.evidence: packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts reproduces packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts almost line for line: the readers allowlist pattern, the non-configurable/non-writable `get` exception, the `batch(fn)` pass-through, and all nine traps (`set`/`defineProperty`/`deleteProperty`/`getPrototypeOf`/`setPrototypeOf`/`preventExtensions`/`isExtensible`/`has`/`getOwnPropertyDescriptor`/`ownKeys`). Only the reader set and the two extras (`HISTORY_METHODS`, the `READ_ONLY_VIEWS` idempotence WeakSet) differ — and those extras are the divergence already: the docs copy has no idempotence and no history-return handling, so the same security-boundary logic now behaves differently per package and future trap fixes must be made twice. The generic part is parameterizable by (readers set, per-member fallbacks) and belongs in `@wafflebase/core`, which is where the repo puts shared engine code. Mitigating context: docs/design/shared-core-extraction.md:46-48 lists "Store abstraction unification" as a Non-Goal — but this is a generic Proxy guard, not a store interface, so that Non-Goal does not obviously cover it.

samples.summary: Design doc's Goals and the index entry still describe the shadow-first rollout the change abandons
samples.evidence: The Summary (line 29) and Rollout (232-241) sections were rewritten to "enforcement is the default", but the Goals list at line 43 still reads "Safe, reversible rollout (shadow/log-only before enforcing)", line 269 still cites a "staged shadow→enforce rollout" as the mitigation for "Bug denies all access", and docs/design/README.md:155 still summarises the doc as "shadow→enforce rollout". Per docs/design/template.md the Goals section is where the decision lives, so a reversal of the rollout posture should be reflected there rather than only in prose further down.

samples.summary: One env var is given two contradictory meanings across the backend
samples.evidence: `isYorkieAuthEnforced` (yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:29) reads unset as *enforcing*, while `assertYorkieAuthEnforced` (template-review.ts:105) and scripts/register-templates.ts:154 require the literal `'true'`. The doc comment defends this as "two different questions", but the consequence is that the intended default deployment (variable unset, methods registered, fully enforcing) is refused the public template tier and cannot run the template seed until it sets a variable that no longer changes webhook behaviour. If the second question is really "were the webhook methods registered?", that deserves its own affirmation (e.g. `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_METHODS_REGISTERED`) rather than overloading a variable whose only remaining code effect is opting *out*.

samples.summary: The "no doc.update() on a read-only mount" rule is implemented as six ad-hoc booleans rather than through the read-only store wrapper the repo already uses
samples.evidence: The same rule is now spelled out separately in YorkieStore's constructor/`updateSelection`/`ensureAxisOrder` (yorkie-store.ts), YorkieDocStore's new `readOnly` field (yorkie-doc-store.ts:590,1263,3196), pdf-collab's `onActivePageChange`, slides-view's `broadcast`, and board-view's selection listener — while the two packages that have a store-level guard (`readOnlyDocStore`, the new `readOnlyNoteStore`) are bypassed for exactly these presence paths (docs-view passes a boolean into the raw `YorkieDocStore` instead of wrapping it). That is the failure shape the task lessons file itself describes ("the guard goes on the listener you were thinking about"): the next presence publish added to any of these stores is unguarded by default. A store-level chokepoint per engine would keep one answer instead of six.

samples.summary: The cross-cutting read-only-mount presence rule this change introduces is not recorded in any canonical design doc
samples.evidence: The change establishes a new invariant across five document types — a read-only (viewer) mount must not reach `doc.update()`, presence and `initialRoot` seeds included, because the next PushPull would carry verb `rw` and be denied. It is written down only in docs/tasks/active/20260907-notes-share-toolbar-lessons.md (a task lessons file) and partially inside notes.md's notes-specific section. Nothing in docs/design/sharing.md, frontend.md, pdf.md, sheets/collaboration.md, slides/slides-collaboration.md or board/board.md states it, so the rule the sheets/slides/board/pdf code now depends on has no canonical home for the next author of a presence publish.
searchedFor: read docs/design/README.md (index of all design docs)

samples.summary: The viewMode/keymap/showAuthors state machine and the mobile `both`→`edit` demotion are copied from notes-detail rather than shared
samples.evidence: shared-notes-layout.tsx:63-78 duplicates notes-detail.tsx:87-139's state trio and re-states the identical demotion rule (`isMobile && viewMode === "both" ? "edit" : viewMode`). The only intended difference is "read the preferences, never write them", which a small shared hook (`useNoteViewPrefs({ persist })`) would express while keeping the demotion single-sourced — notes-toolbar.tsx's own comment now has to name both routes to stay accurate.

samples.summary: Unrelated jsdom test-teardown fixes bundled into the change
samples.evidence: The editor-disposal collectors added to packages/docs/test/view/large-paste-indicator.test.ts and update-style-to-match.test.ts fix a CI coverage-run flake in the docs package that has no connection to the notes share-link issue or to the auth-webhook work. verdict.reason: The bundling premise is real (the branch does flip the enforcement default alongside the notes-toolbar issue), but the finding's blocking rationale is contradicted by the tree. (1) The claimed missing migration step exists: self-hosting.md:185 and :584-605 document "unset (**enforce**)" plus a three-step rollout window ("Deploy with YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=false ... Confirm the logs show no false denials ... Unset the variable") and a CAUTION block; backend/README.md:101-108 and :263-270 say the same; docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:231-243 keeps shadow as an explicit opt-in rollout step and states it is "Reversible at every step". (2) The claimed inconsistency with assertYorkieAuthEnforced is a documented deliberate decision, not a defect: template-review.ts:61-112 explains that the === 'true' gate is intentionally stricter because it asserts the operator affirmed the Yorkie-side method registration, which no env default can observe (repeated at self-hosting.md:625-631). (3) No stated Non-Goal is crossed: yorkie-auth-webhook.md:34-52 lists server-enforced per-document authorization as a Goal, and enforcement was already a recorded release precondition (20260905-release-v0.6.9-todo.md:79-88, 20260902-revision-history-todo.md:34). All N1-N8 acceptance items are present and checked (20260907-notes-share-toolbar-todo.md:12-37), and the docs were folded into the canonical subsystem doc rather than a parallel one. Under this lens none of the major triggers apply (no unmet acceptance criterion, no duplicated logic that will diverge, no Non-Goal breach); what remains is PR-hygiene/scope bundling whose cost stays inside the repo's own process, which the rubric grades minor and therefore non-blocking.
